newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Prices drift, but buyers emerging.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Prices drift, but buyers emerging.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices drifted this week amid a fall in Taiwan tender prices, but buyers were starting to emerge for April barrels, industry sources said on Wednesday.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought 7,000 tonnes of MTBE for April 6-20 delivery at $280-$283 per tonne cost-and-freight Taiwan, from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), industry sources said.
A CPC official told Reuters around five offers had been received for the tender, which closed March 3 and sought the MTBE for delivery to Kaohsiung and Keelung.
The official said the price was reasonable and lower than CPC's last tender for March 1-15 delivery at $283 c-and-f.
Trader sentiment was however mixed on the award and the short-term outlook for prices.

"Essentially the price reflects the prices in the U.S. Gulf and the lack of demand in the region," a trader said. "There are no spot buyers so I don't see how prices can firm unless U.S. prices improve."
Prices in the U.S. Gulf have recently slumped under the weight of ample supplies, traders said.
Taking this and Taiwan's award into consideration, Singapore free-on-board (fob) April MTBE was being offered as low as $268-$270 per tonne down from $270-$273 last week.
Suppliers saw support for the market however on the back of the strong Asian gasoline market.
"It (Taiwan's award) is a lousy price for the seller," a producer said. "Gasoline is so good .. the current MTBE octane value is higher than the spot value of MTBE."
Singapore fob 95-octane gasoline prices rose $2.00 per barrel to $28.60 by Tuesday from late last week.
Although no spot MTBE trade has been reported in the last week, buyers have started to emerge from Indonesia and Thailand for April supplies, the producer said.
Buyers have not yet indicated bid levels, but the producer said buyers would probably be willing to pay as high as $275 per tonne fob, he said.
Taiwan's reformate cargo imports would also spur demand in April, sources said.
CPC's tender for 250,000 barrels of leaded and unleaded reformate with a 2.0-pct MTBE requirement for April 1-15, closed March 4 and offers are valid until March 6.
